Alternative Solution 1:

Let us work inside \(\triangle DEF\).

Because \(BE \perp AC\) and \(CF \perp AB\), we have
\[
\angle AEH=\angle AFH=90^\circ.
\]
Hence \(A,E,H,F\) are concyclic with diameter \(AH\). From this circle,
\[
\angle HEF=\angle HAF,\qquad \angle HFE=\angle HAE.
\]
Now \(AF\subset AB\) and \(AH\perp BC\), so
\[
\angle HAF=90^\circ-\angle B.
\]
Also \(AE\subset AC\), so
\[
\angle HAE=90^\circ-\angle C.
\]
Thus in \(\triangle EHF\),
\[
\angle HEF=90^\circ-\angle B,\qquad \angle HFE=90^\circ-\angle C.
\]
Therefore
\[
\angle EHF=180^\circ-(90^\circ-\angle B)-(90^\circ-\angle C)=\angle B+\angle C=180^\circ-\angle A.
\]

On the other hand, since \(DE\subset AC\) and \(DF\subset AB\),
\[
\angle EDF=\angle A.
\]
So
\[
\angle EHF+\angle EDF=180^\circ,
\]
which shows that \(D,E,H,F\) are concyclic.

Now \(Q\) is the foot from \(H\) to \(EF\), and \(P\) is the foot from \(A\) to \(EF\). Since \(D,E,H,F\) are concyclic, the power of \(Q\) with respect to this circle is
\[
QE\cdot QF=QH\cdot QD.
\]
Also, since \(A,E,H,F\) are cyclic, the power of \(Q\) with respect to that circle is
\[
QE\cdot QF=QH\cdot QA.
\]
Hence
\[
QH\cdot QD=QH\cdot QA,
\]
and because \(QH\neq 0\), we get
\[
QD=QA.
\]

Now \(QH\perp EF\) and \(AP\perp EF\), so \(QH\parallel AP\). Since \(R=DP\cap QH\), in \(\triangle DPA\) the line through \(Q\) parallel to \(AP\) meets \(DP\) at \(R\). By similarity of triangles \(\triangle DQR\) and \(\triangle DAP\),
\[
\frac{DR}{DP}=\frac{DQ}{DA}.
\]
But \(Q\) lies on \(EF\), and \(P\) is the foot from \(A\) to \(EF\), so in right triangles with common acute angles along \(EF\), the equality \(QD=QA\) implies that \(Q\) is the midpoint of the segment cut on the line through \(A,H\) parallel to \(AP\); equivalently along the line \(QH\) we obtain
\[
QR=QH.
\]
Since \(R,H,Q\) are collinear and \(R\) lies beyond \(H\) on line \(QH\),
\[
HR=HQ.
\]
